source_text:
Στίχ. ιδ΄. Καὶ ἀπῆρε πᾶς λαὸς ἐκ τῶν σκηνωμάτων αὐτῶν.
Τουτέστιν, ὡς ἅλω πλήρωσις (69). Οὐ γὰρ μόνον ἐπήγνυτο, ὡς ἐν τῇ Ἐρυθρᾷ, ἀλλʼ ὡς θημὼν πυροῦ ἐσωρεύετο. Εἰς τύπον τῶν ἀποστόλων δηλονότι.
thought_title: The Jordan piled like a heap of wheat as a type of the apostles
orientation: Origen begins his commentary on Joshua 3:14, explaining what the departure of the people from their tents means.
pass_a_gloss: Verse 14. And all the people departed from their tents. That is, as a floor [is] fullness. For not only was it congealed, as in the Red [Sea], but as a heap of wheat it was heaped up. As a type of the apostles, clearly.

choices.why: The phrase is elliptical; 'floor' renders ἅλω as threshing floor, and 'fullness' keeps the noun πλήρωσις literally, with the copula supplied in brackets.
rejected: as full as a threshing floor
like the fullness of a threshing floor

choices.why: The verb πήγνυμι means to fix or make solid; 'congealed' preserves the physical solidification of water implied by the contrast with heaping.
The glossary requires 'heap of wheat' for this fixed image.
The passive imperfect of σωρεύω conveys an ongoing piling action done to the waters, matching the image of a heap.

choices.english: As a type of the apostles, clearly
choices.why: δηλονότι is an adverbial clarifier; placing 'clearly' at the end preserves its emphatic, parenthetical force.
rejected: obviously as a type of the apostles
that is, as a type of the apostles

bible_refs.note: Καὶ ἀπῆρε πᾶς λαὸς ἐκ τῶν σκηνωμάτων αὐτῶν

pass_b_english: “And all the people departed from their tents” (Joshua 3:14). That is, as a threshing floor is full. For the water was not merely congealed, as at the Red Sea, but was heaped up like a heap of wheat—clearly as a type of the apostles.

problems.quote: as a threshing floor is full
problems.why: Phrase seems incomplete or mistranslated; doesn't connect to wheat heap clearly
problems.fix: Check Latin: may mean 'as a threshing floor is full of grain'

problems.quote: That is, as a threshing floor is full.
problems.why: This clause has no clear connection to the preceding quotation about people departing from tents.
problems.fix: Likely a gloss on the multitude of people; needs a connecting verb or explanation.

edits.old: That is, as a threshing floor is full.
edits.new: That is, as a threshing floor is full of grain.

fixed: Added 'of grain' to clarify the simile: the source has ὡς ἅλω πλήρωσις, 'as a floor fullness,' which is elliptical; the fuller sense is a threshing floor full of grain, connecting to the heap of wheat that follows.
The clause is a gloss on the people departing, not on the water; the source's elliptical phrase is clarified by the addition, so no further change is needed.
